name: Graph and Graph
description: You are given two connected undirected graphs with the same number of vertices. In both graphs, there is a token located at some vertex. In the first graph, the token is initially at vertex $$$s_1$$$, and in the second graph, the token is initially at vertex $$$s_2$$$. The following operation is repeated an infinite number of times: Let the token currently be at vertex $$$v_1$$$ in the first graph and at vertex $$$v_2$$$ in the second graph. A vertex $$$u_1$$$, adjacent to $$$v_1$$$, is chosen in the first graph. A vertex $$$u_2$$$, adjacent to $$$v_2$$$, is chosen in the second graph. The tokens are moved to the chosen vertices: in the first graph, the token moves from $$$v_1$$$ to $$$u_1$$$, and in the second graph, from $$$v_2$$$ to $$$u_2$$$. The cost of such an operation is equal to $$$|u_1 - u_2|$$$. Determine the minimum possible total cost of all operations or report that this value will be infinitely large.
input_specification: Each test consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 500$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$s_1$$$, and $$$s_2$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 1000$$$, $$$1 \le s_1, s_2 \le n$$$) — the number of vertices in each graph, the number of the vertex in the first graph where the token is initially located, and the number of the vertex in the second graph where the token is initially located. The second line of each test case contains one integer $$$m_1$$$ ($$$1 \le m_1 \le 1000$$$) — the number of edges in the first graph. The $$$i$$$-th of the following $$$m_1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$a_i$$$ and $$$b_i$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i, b_i \le n$$$, $$$a_i \ne b_i$$$) — the numbers of the endpoints of the $$$i$$$-th edge in the first graph. The next line of each test case contains one integer $$$m_2$$$ ($$$1 \le m_2 \le 1000$$$) — the number of edges in the second graph. The $$$j$$$-th of the following $$$m_2$$$ lines contains two integers $$$c_j$$$ and $$$d_j$$$ ($$$1 \le c_j, d_j \le n$$$, $$$c_j \ne d_j$$$) — the numbers of the endpoints of the $$$j$$$-th edge in the second graph. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$, the sum of $$$m_1$$$, and the sum of $$$m_2$$$ over all test cases do not exceed $$$1000$$$. It is guaranteed that both graphs are connected.
output_specification: For each test case, output one integer — the minimum total cost of all operations or $$$-1$$$, if this value will be infinitely large.
approach_summary: Formulate the state transition graph with non-negative weights. Execute Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue to find shortest paths in O((V + E) log V).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2059D — Graph and Graph [168. Dijkstra's Algorithm]
topic_editorial.summary: Single-source shortest path using Dijkstra's algorithm.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Because all edge weights are non-negative, the shortest distance to the unvisited vertex with the minimum tentative distance is finalized and cannot be decreased by further transitions (greedy choice property).
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Graph Modeling
Construct an adjacency list with pairs $(v, w)$ for each directed or undirected edge from $u$ to $v$ with weight $w \ge 0$.

### Step 2: Distance Table Initialization
Initialize $dist[v] = \infty$ for all vertices, with $dist[\text{source}] = 0$.
Push $(0, \text{source})$ into a min-priority queue `std::priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>>`.

### Step 3: Relaxation Loop
While the priority queue is not empty:
1. Pop $(d, u)$. If $d > dist[u]$, discard (stale entry).
2. For each neighbor $(v, w)$ of $u$:
   If $dist[u] + w < dist[v]$:
   $$dist[v] = dist[u] + w$$
   Push $(dist[v], v)$ into the priority queue.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((V + E) \log V)$
  Every vertex is extracted from the priority queue at most once. For every edge, we perform at most one priority queue push operation taking $\mathcal{O}(\log V)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(V + E)$
  Required for storing the adjacency list and the distance array.
